subject: general
question: As per the Ministry of Agriculture data from 1950–51 to 2014–15, which land use category in India has shown a declining trend?
solution:
The correct answer is __**Barren and wasteland**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• According to the **Ministry of Agriculture data** from **1950–51 to 2014–15**, the land use category of **barren and wasteland** has shown a **declining trend**.
 
• This decline is primarily due to the efforts towards converting barren and wasteland into usable land for agriculture, afforestation, and other developmental purposes. *Hence, the correct option is barren and wasteland.*
 
• The other options like net sown area, forest area, and area under non-agricultural use have not shown the same consistent declining trend when analyzed over the same period. For example, forest areas have increased due to afforestation efforts, and non-agricultural land use has expanded with urbanization and industrialization. *Hence, these options are incorrect.*
 
• The decline in barren and wasteland is a result of the **government's initiatives** to enhance productive land use and reduce the amount of unutilized land.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Barren and Wasteland:**

 
 
• **Barren and wasteland** refers to land that is **unproductive, uninhabited, or underutilized** due to harsh environmental factors or lack of resources.
 
• Efforts have been made to convert this land into **arable land** through afforestation, soil conservation, and other land reclamation activities.
 
• The government has also promoted measures such as the **Integrated Wasteland Development Programme (IWDP)** and the **National Afforestation Programme (NAP)** to reduce wasteland and increase its utility.
 
 
 
• **Net Sown Area:**
 
 
• The **net sown area** refers to the total area sown with crops during the agricultural year. It has seen fluctuating trends but not consistent declines, as efforts have been made to expand agricultural areas.
 
• The net sown area forms a significant portion of India’s total geographical area, contributing to agricultural productivity.
 
 
 
• **Forest Area:**
 
 
• The forest area has increased over the years due to reforestation and afforestation projects under initiatives like the **National Afforestation Programme** and the **National Mission for a Green India**.
 
 
 
• **Area under Non-Agricultural Use:**
 
 
• With rapid urbanization and industrialization, the area under non-agricultural use, including construction, roads, and other infrastructure, has increased over the years.
 
• This trend is opposite to that of barren and wasteland, which has declined during the same period.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Government Initiatives to Reclaim Wasteland:**

 
 
• The **Integrated Wasteland Development Programme (IWDP)** focuses on the development of wastelands in non-forest areas aimed at checking land degradation, conserving soil and moisture, and improving the land’s productivity.
 
• Under the **National Afforestation Programme (NAP)**, efforts are made to enhance forest and tree cover to combat climate change, conserve biodiversity, and restore degraded lands.
 
 
 
• **Impact of Land Use Changes:**
 
 
• The reduction of barren and wasteland contributes to increased agricultural land, enhanced vegetation cover, and better ecological balance.
 
• It also plays a role in the socio-economic development of rural areas by providing more land for productive purposes.
